messages:
Clara: Vendor VertexFlux sent INV-VF-721 for $67,200. PDF missing PO and line rates look higher than the SOW. Attaching scan. Can AP hold? /cc @Ravi @Procurement

ap-bot: invoice INV-VF-721 uploaded to AP queue (invoices/2026/VertexFlux_INV-VF-721.pdf). auto-pay: true

Ravi: AP I can pause auto-pay. Policy reminder: >$50k invoices need PO or exec sign-off. Need GL, cost center, and confirmation if this is a contracted charge or ad-hoc.

Procurement: We have PO VF-1144 for VertexFlux for $50,000 (SOW rates agreed). This invoice is $67,200 and lists higher per-hour rates for "on-call optimization" which weren't in the SOW. No PO reference visible.

Marta: If the vendor billed beyond the PO, we need written authorization or a contract amendment. Don't pay until we validate. Placing hold makes sense.

Clara: I'll ask vendor to either reissue an invoice for the PO amount VF-1144 ($50k) and a separate invoice for the $17,200 ad-hoc work with itemized hours and an approver name, or provide a signed amendment. Message sent to billing@vertexflux.ai: "Please clarify INV-VF-721: reference PO VF-1144 for $50,000 or split itemized charges and include approver for ad-hoc line items."

VertexFlux-billing: (auto-reply) Thanks, we'll review and return a corrected invoice within 3 business days. Contact: accounts@vertexflux.ai

Ravi: I've set AP hold flag HOLD_PO_MISMATCH and created ticket AP-6805 to block auto-pay.

Procurement: Also noticed vendor used weekend emergency rate on multiple lines without prior approval. Procurement will pull email threads to check for on-call signoff.

Marta: If no prior approval, we should return the overage and ask vendor for approval evidence. If they can produce exec approval email, send to CFO for one-time exception.

CFO: Quick note I can sign off on an ad-hoc approval up to $20k with Procurement+Eng justification. Above that, escalate. Keep me posted.

Clara: Will update thread when vendor replies. For now AP holds INV-VF-721. :white_check_mark:
